section_1.heading: Introduction
section_1.text:
Zika virus (ZIKV) is an arbovirus belonging to the family Flaviviridae, and is closely related to the dengue, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis, and West Nile viruses. It was first isolated from a monkey in the Zika forest of Uganda in 1947

ZIKV is primarily transmitted by the bites of infectious Aedes mosquitoes

With the ease of modern transportation, there is a potential that the ZIKV outbreak may become a global public health crisis.

In this work, we present a compartmental model for ZIKV based on SEIR host model and SEI vector model, using logistic growth in human population and dynamic vector population

section_2.heading: Method and Design
section_2.text:
The compartmental model consists of two parts: the compartments for human, subscripted with HH; and compartments for vectors, subscripted with VV. Although there have been a few reported deaths related to ZIKV, most ZIKV cases only result in mild symptoms among infectious individuals. We use an SEIR (Susceptible, Exposed, Infectious, Recovered) model to describe the disease spread among the human population. Let SS HH (tt), EE HH (tt), II HH (tt) and RR HH (tt) denote the number of individuals in each compartment at time tt. The human population at time t is given as NN HH (tt) = SS HH (tt) + II HH (tt) + EE HH (tt) + RR HH (tt). During the outbreak, the human population is assumed to follow a logistic growth with carrying capacity KK HH.

The compartments for vectors consist of both the infectious status and the life stages of the mosquito. In particular, a typical life cycle of a mosquito has four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult. Let VV 1 (tt), VV 2 (tt) and VV 3 (tt) denote the number of eggs, larvae, and pupae of vectors in the environment. Since only female adults bite humans and transmit the virus, there are no infectious compartments for these three stages. Let SS VV (tt), EE VV (tt) and II VV (tt) denote the number of susceptible, exposed, and infectious female adults in the environment at time tt, and denote the total female vector population as NN VV (tt) = SS VV (tt) + II VV (tt) + EE VV (tt). Due to their short life cycle, the birth and death rate of vector population is taken into consideration. The transmission from susceptible to infectious in both human and vector population is associated with mosquito bites. Figure
